intent: A weather reporter standing in the dark: calm numbers that keep getting more absurd, one shiver per sentence.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: The COLDEST inhabited place on Earth is in which country?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: The coldest inhabited place on Earth is in which country?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Russia. A tiny village deep in eastern Siberia dropped below minus 67 degrees in 1933, still the record.

lines.direction: tight on the village: the Oymyakon pin is already there, Yakutsk pins to the west as the nearest city, a cold-face sticker pops on 'people', then the January counter falls 0 → −46 while the frost sticker lands
lines.text: Around 500 people still live there, and a perfectly normal January averages minus 46.

lines.direction: the scale: a 3-row bar chart grows over the dark Siberian interior — freezer, Oymyakon, Vostok — the ice-cube sticker pops on 'freezer', Russia pulses on 'colder', the penguin lands on 'vostok'
lines.text: Your kitchen freezer sits at minus 18. Only Antarctica, where nobody actually lives, goes any colder.

lines.direction: back to the village: the SCHOOL OPEN card slams in on 'school', the school sticker pops, the Oymyakon pin pulses, the cool Russia flag-ball reacts on 'older'
lines.text: And the village school stays open until minus 52, which most of us would call a snow day.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Pack a second coat. Follow us.
